evidence: Preface (PDF p.22): "Appendix A numbers its own sections with a letter suffix, so Appendix A § 9A means Appendix A, the section labelled 9A" — but the same page also says "Appendix A, A.6 carries a boxed 2026-09-27 capability probe" and "a superseding re-verification of the DeepSeek model-service status (Appendix A, A.3)"; Ch. 4 Table 4-2 note (PDF p.75): "Appendix A's §A.7 (Fig A.2, vendor-relative KV/compute ratios)"; Ch. 1 (PDF p.27): "all accessed 2026-08-30, the book's evidence cutoff; Appendix A §10"; Ch. 3 (PDF p.76): "model card HF Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, accessed 2026-08-30; A.10".
issue: Three mutually inconsistent reference forms are used for one class of target — Appendix A's own section numbers: "§ 9A" (number-then-letter, which the Preface defines as the scheme), "A.3 / A.6 / A.7 / A.10" (letter-then-number) and a bare "§10". Under the convention the Preface states, "§10" and "A.10" do not resolve to a "9A"-style label, and a reader cannot tell whether they name the same section. The same prefix is also used for figure numbers ("Fig A.2") and section numbers ("§A.7"), which compounds the ambiguity. This is a cross-reference defect that will not resolve for a reader navigating Appendix A.
fix_instruction: Choose one appendix-section label scheme (e.g. "§ A.10", "§ A.7") and normalise every occurrence to it — including the Preface's definition of "§ 9A" and the bare "§10" in Ch. 1 — or, if "9A" is a genuinely distinct subsection label, print the full scheme (section number + subsection letter) once in the Preface and map the A.N references onto it.

chapter: Ch. 4 — The Anatomy of an AI Workload
evidence: PDF p.96: "Time basis: this is the rate over the active business-hours window (an 8-hour × 260-workday schedule), not 24×7 wall-clock." Three lines later, the same page: "Over 24×7 the same 10 rps would extrapolate to ~18.7M requests/month on the same 260-workday calendar (10 × 3,600 × 24 × 260/12 = 18,720,000) — 3× the active-hours volume — or ~9,360 requests/user/month for 2,000 users".
issue: The same quantity is labelled "not 24×7 wall-clock" and then "Over 24×7". The parenthetical arithmetic is 24 hours per *workday* on a 260-workday calendar (520 h/mo), i.e. 18.72M requests/month; a true 24×7 basis on a 730-hour month is 10 × 3,600 × 730 = 26,280,000 (~26.28M requests/month), ~40% higher. The label therefore misdescribes the basis it is attached to, in a paragraph whose whole purpose is to prevent an hour-basis mismatch — the same class of error the book flags elsewhere (e.g. the 730-hour vs 173.33-active-hour spend mismatch).
fix_instruction: Rename the case to what it is — "24 hours a day on the same 260-workday calendar" (or "all wall-clock hours on workdays") — and, if a genuine 24×7 comparison is wanted, add it separately as ~26.28M requests/month (10 × 3,600 × 730).
